claims.claim_vi: The source names six multithreading design patterns: Producer-Consumer, Thread pool, Futures and Promises, Monitor object, Barrier and Read-write lock. Only the names are reused; the lesson explains each pattern from Python and JDK documentation.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Python queue module: it implements multi-producer, multi-consumer queues, especially useful in threaded programming when information must be exchanged safely between multiple threads; the Queue class implements all the required locking semantics.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Python concurrent.futures: ThreadPoolExecutor is an Executor subclass that uses a pool of at most max_workers threads to execute calls asynchronously, is often used to overlap I/O instead of CPU work, and it is recommended not to use it for long-running tasks; the Future class encapsulates the asynchronous execution of a callable and is created by Executor.submit.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Python threading.Barrier: a simple synchronization primitive for a fixed number of threads that need to wait for each other; each thread calls wait and blocks until all have called wait, at which point they are released simultaneously; the barrier can be reused any number of times for the same number of threads.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: JDK Object class documentation: only one thread at a time can own an object's monitor, and a thread becomes the owner by executing a synchronized instance method of the object, the body of a synchronized statement on the object, or, for objects of type Class, a static synchronized method of that class.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: JDK ReadWriteLock: it maintains a pair of associated locks, one for read-only operations and one for writing; the read lock may be held simultaneously by multiple reader threads so long as there are no writers; the write lock is exclusive; a thread acquiring the read lock sees all updates made before the write lock was released.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: The background paragraph (threads share memory, race conditions depend on the order the threads run) and the meaning of promise as the side that promises the result are the author's general knowledge.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge; not checked against primary documentation.

design_notes_vi: Sáu mẫu chia thành hai nhóm (chia việc và lấy kết quả; bảo vệ và đồng bộ). Không có mũi tên vì nguồn không nói thứ tự giữa các mẫu. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source gives a short introduction and one sentence per pattern in one flat order; the lesson keeps only the six names, groups them into two sets by what they do and writes its own explanation of each pattern from the Python queue, concurrent.futures and threading documentation and the JDK Object and ReadWriteLock sources instead of translating the source sentences.
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết trong kho này, chờ review kỹ thuật. Phần giải thích dựa vào tài liệu Python và JDK ở các commit cố định; phần nền và nghĩa của promise là kiến thức chung của người biên soạn, chưa đối chiếu với tài liệu chuẩn. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
